title: When 85% Grammar Scores Were Actually a Coin Flip | vitalii.no
description:
A kids' learning app's own dashboard said grammar was going well: scores in the 70s and 80s, lesson after lesson. But a wrong round could just be retried until it passed, so the headline number was hiding what was really happening underneath.

A closer look at the raw answers, not the retried scores, told a different story. On first-try grammar answers, accuracy sat at 49.9 to 56 percent against a 50 percent guessing floor - statistically no different from a coin flip over 756 answers. Reading gaps were only slightly better, and a strict number comparison had been marking a correct decimal answer wrong, forcing 1121 out of 1121 numeric answers into whole numbers.

The fix replaced free-text answer labels with 420 closed-vocabulary skills tied directly to curriculum aims, added one comparison function used everywhere that accepts decimals and fractions, and switched grammar from pick-the-right-answer recognition to typed correction. A wrong typed answer is now re-asked as multiple choice and logged honestly as a second try, not a plain miss.

The result: maths mistakes now get corrected on a retry 65 percent of the time, up from just 16 percent before the fix.
